small_guidance:
- The current kernel re-loads the same weight `w_v` four times per (kh,kw) but uses it across 4 spatial offsets — that's fine, but the inner `for ic in range(0, IC)` is not unrolled and reloads weights one OC-vector at a time. Tile the IC loop with `BLOCK_IC` (e.g. 8 or 16) and use `tl.dot` on `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] @ [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_HW]` per (kh,kw) — this turns the kernel into a real GEMM and uses tensor cores effectively.
- Add larger autotune configs once IC is tiled, e.g. `(BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_HW=64, BLOCK_IC=16, num_warps=4)` and `(BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_HW=64, BLOCK_IC=8, num_warps=8)`; verify SMEM `(BM·BK + BK·BN)·4·stages ≲ 132KB`.
- Switch input layout to NHWC (`channels_last`) so the IC dimension is contiguous — this lets a single `tl.load` fetch `BLOCK_IC` channels coalesced and is the precondition for the GEMM tiling above.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile)`, with the K dimension being `IC*KH*KW` (or `IC` inside a static `KH*KW` loop). Use `tl.dot` to accumulate `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] x [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_HW]` for each of the 4 pre-pool positions; the current scalar `w_v[:,None] * x_v[None,:]` outer-product path leaves tensor cores idle and is the main reason fast_p≈0.51.
- Fuse the 2x2 maxpool by computing only the 4 conv outputs needed per pooled location (already done) but make the pooled-spatial tile the GEMM-N tile and keep the 4 accumulators `acc00/01/10/11` across the K-loop with `tl.dot` — then reduce + hardswish + mish in the epilogue exactly once.
- Convert input/weight to NHWC / `(OC, KH, KW, IC)` layout at init (cache on the module) so the K-axis is contiguous; this enables vectorized 128-bit loads along IC and removes the per-(kh,kw) gather scalar pattern.
